newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Taiwan futures end firmer on second day.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Taiwan futures end firmer on second day.

text.p: Newly launched Taiwan stock index futures traded in Singapore ended firmer on Friday in line with the cash market, but volume stayed thin, dealers said.
The contract faced competition from Chicago, which launched its own Taiwan futures index on Thursday, but was still drawing curious investors, they said.
"Locals may end up doing most of the trade if Taiwanese investors continue to be discouraged from trading futures," one Japanese commission house dealer said.
The March futures contract closed at 308.9, clawing its way back from an opening 306.5 tracking the cash market.
Volume fell to 371 lots, compared with Thursday's estimated 500 contracts.
Dealers said earlier the contract's tight three-point range made it difficult to trade.
"When I look at the cash market, it's bullish, inviting buyers to come in whenever there's a dip. But so far, there's been no dip," said a trader with a local institution.
He said the contract faced fairly strong resistance at its high of 311.0, established on Thursday, and a break above that level could push it higher.
The Taiwan Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) cash index, on which the SIMEX futures contract is based, settled on Friday at 312.04 points, up 3.23.

One commission house chartist said the contract held an upward bias helped by views that Taiwan's economy was strong and contract would attract new business. But weakness in regional indices like Japan's Nikkei and Hong Hong's Hang Seng may eventually pressure Taiwan's market.
"Most of the indices in the world are coming down, and Wall Street is at a peak. Overall, (Taiwan) won't be able to shake the bearish sentiment," he said.
On Friday, strong buying in electronics during the final hour pulled the Taiwan stock index to a sharply higher finish, with the index expected soon to try resistance at 7,200 points.
